solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, mirror symmetry); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Take a spin when going out?

definitions.text: Take a spin when going out?

parts.words: Take a spin when going out?
parts.note: 'going out' suggests leaving the house for a drive, but it means dropping off into deep slumber, which a spinning toy does motionlessly

explanation.surface: Someone planning a quick drive in the car on their way out for the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: A spinning top that is perfectly balanced looks completely still, hence the idiom for very sound slumber; 'going out' is the colloquial sense of losing consciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes slumbering soundly, and 'going out' is slang for falling asleep, so a well-spun top is the image.

clue.text: Fielder to die of frustration, primarily

parts.note: to be dying for something is to long for it

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the word frustration only

explanation.surface: A cricketer in the outfield is close to expiring from exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: Long off is a cricket fielding position, deep on the off side behind the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Long off is a fielding position in cricket, so the name stands for the player stationed there.

clue.text: Each accent getting cut: all of the French pine away

parts.note: EA is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price labels
an accent or way of speaking can be called a tone
to shear is to cut, as with wool
tout is the French word for all

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson in which every French accent mark is lopped off, and the language mourns.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat one's heart out is an idiom for grieving or yearning in silence, the same as wasting with longing.

clue.text: Clearly in a fortunate way, bagging 500 (not 1000)

indicators.note: bagging means putting something into a bag, so one piece is placed inside another
not tells us the item named in the brackets is dropped from the word

parts.note: to act in a fortunate way is to do so luckily
K stands for a thousand, from kilo
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: Plainly someone was lucky to pocket a modest sum, though not the larger one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not 1000' strips K from LUCKILY to leave LUCILY, and 'bagging' then puts D inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucidly is an adverb meaning in a clear, easily understood way, matching plainly.

clue.text: Equipment left to fall out of Scottish garb

indicators.note: to fall out of something is to leave it, so a letter departs from the word

parts.note: the kilt is the traditional Scottish skirt-like garment

explanation.surface: Some gear has been allowed to drop from a Highlander's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit is a general word for gear, the set of things needed for a sport or job.

clue.text: Some warfare melded with tall tale by an American

indicators.note: melded means blended together, so these letters are merged and rearranged

explanation.surface: A war story embellished into a tall tale by a writer from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is all of SOME WARFARE plus TALL, fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's novel of the First World War is a story by a US author, hence a tale by an American.

clue.text: Describe a switch in positions for rugby throw

indicators.note: a switch in positions means the two halves of the word swap places

parts.note: a lineout is the rugby restart where the ball is thrown in between two lines of players

explanation.surface: Explain a tactical swap of players for a throw-in on the rugby pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby union restarts play after the ball goes out with a throw between two lines of forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To outline something is to sketch it in words, giving its main points, which is to describe it.

clue.text: Fool curtailed meal, coming round when it's eaten?

indicators.note: coming round means encircling, so the shortened meal wraps around other letters
curtailed means having its tail cut off, losing its final letter

parts.note: lunch is the midday meal
the midday meal is traditionally taken at one o'clock, written AT I

explanation.surface: A silly person bolts a shortened meal and then wonders when exactly it was consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when it's eaten' refers back to the meal: lunch is eaten at one, AT I with I as one.
explanation.definitionFit: Lunatic, as a noun, is an informal term for a madman or idiot, so it can stand for a fool.

clue.text: One ear getting good with time? Such cases aren't seen about

parts.note: lug is British slang for an ear, and one of the pair is the left one
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An ear improving over the years, and some cases that are never seen around.
explanation.walkthrough: The left-luggage office at a British railway station stores bags deposited by travellers; such cases are not carried about.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags handed in at a depot and left behind are not toted around, so they are suitcases out of circulation.

clue.text: Foremost of two-timers or rat, I fancy

definitions.text: Foremost of two-timers or rat, I fancy

indicators.note: foremost of picks out the front letter of the next word only
fancy as a verb means imagine, and as an adjective means elaborate, here signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker reckons the chief double-crosser, or rat, is a betrayer.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a two-timer or rat is a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-timers and rats are both informal words for people who betray others, which is what a betrayer does.

clue.text: Danger light flickered, showing abrupt change of direction

indicators.note: something flickered moves unsteadily, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A warning lamp blinked as a vehicle swerved sharply.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-angled bend turns through ninety degrees, an abrupt change of course.

clue.text: Father to have a threatening look

parts.note: FR is the abbreviation for Father as a priest's title
to own something is to have it

explanation.surface: Dad shoots a menacing glance.
explanation.definitionFit: A frown is a scowl, a furrowed brow showing displeasure or menace.

clue.text: Unresolved, central character taking lead, becoming more intense

indicators.note: taking lead means going to the front, so that part moves to the start
the central character of the word for unresolved is its middle letter, written out in full as a letter name

parts.note: something unresolved is still pending

explanation.surface: An undecided story whose hero steps forward as tension builds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'central character' is D, spelt out as its name DEE; 'taking lead' moves DEE to the front of PENING. The bloggers queried spelling D as DEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Deepening, as a participle, describes something growing stronger or more profound.

clue.text: Rising foreign drama existed in Utopian state

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from the bottom up, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Noh is the classical masked drama of Japan
existed means were, in the plural past

explanation.surface: Overseas theatre on the up in a perfect land.
explanation.walkthrough: Erewhon is Samuel Butler's satirical imagined country, its name nearly 'nowhere' backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Butler's novel describes an imaginary commonwealth, a satirical ideal land like More's Utopia.

clue.text: Story about spirited Liberal abandoning one sort of behaviour

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for story goes round the rest

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: feisty means lively and spirited
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the abbreviation for Liberal in politics

explanation.surface: A tale concerning a lively politician who walks out on a colleague.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' signals dropping the one (I); the Liberal's L joins the trimmed adjective, and 'about' puts the whole lot inside the fib. 'sort of behaviour' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifestyle is the way a person habitually lives, a pattern of conduct.

clue.text: Energy escape is something attracting attention

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics
a vent is an outlet, an escape for air or steam

explanation.surface: A burst of power escaping catches everyone's eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is an occasion or happening, something notable that draws people's notice.

clue.text: UK territory's mistake about Queen? Nonsense

parts.note: Gib is the familiar short name for Gibraltar, a British Overseas Territory

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for mistake goes round the royal letters

parts.note: bish is British slang for a blunder
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A British outpost blunders over the monarch, which seems absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: GIBRALTAR, at Spain's southern tip, is a British territory, often called Gib; BISH is old British slang for a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Gibberish is meaningless talk, a synonym for drivel or rubbish.

clue.text: Italian city work unit taking a month to shore up left side of bank

indicators.note: in a down entry, shoring something up means sitting beneath it as a prop
the left side of a written word is its opening letter

parts.note: the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Builders spend a month propping up a riverbank in Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergamo is a city in Lombardy, northern Italy, near Milan.

clue.text: One's enthralled by popular epithet for now

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: enthralled by means held captive by, so one letter is held inside a word

parts.note: a term is a word or name, like an epithet
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone captivated by a fashionable nickname, for the time being.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim describes something temporary, lasting only until a permanent arrangement, so it stands for provisionally.

clue.text: End of sonnet material

definitions.meaning: a sonnet has fourteen lines; labelled from A

explanation.surface: The close of a poem and some cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: N is the fourteenth letter, so if the lines are lettered A onward the last line of a fourteen-line poem is LINE N.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is cloth made from flax fibres, a common textile.

clue.text: African city atmosphere constrained by no sexual orientation

indicators.note: constrained by means held in, so one piece sits inside another

parts.note: taken as written
air is the atmosphere
bi is short for bisexual, a sexual orientation

explanation.surface: A city whose air is restricted by having no orientation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital of Kenya, in East Africa.

clue.text: Song that's penned about horse?

indicators.note: penned means shut in a pen, so the song encloses the short word for about

parts.note: an air is a tune or song
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A ballad written about a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' looks like an animal, but it is the clothes horse, a frame for drying washing.
explanation.definitionFit: An airer is a clothes horse, a folding rack on which laundry is hung to dry.

clue.text: Barber's a great many over to test getting trimmed on top

parts.note: tons means lots, a great many
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

indicators.note: trimmed on top means cut at the head, losing the first letter

parts.note: a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A barber getting a client's hair trimmed on top for the umpteenth time.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonsorial is an adjective relating to hairdressers and their work, so it means of a barber.

clue.text: United in glamour, reflecting no end of mystic charm

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the letter for United goes within the rest
reflecting means mirrored, so the letters are read in reverse order
no means without, so the letter that follows is removed

parts.note: romance is glamour or exciting mystery

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word mystic

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A team in a glamorous setting, mirroring a mystic's enchantment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of mystic' drops C from ROMANCE to leave ROMANE; 'reflecting' turns it to ENAMOR, and U goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to captivate or fill with love, which is to bewitch or delight.

clue.text: Fighter's promise to involve a couple of sides

indicators.note: to involve is to include or take in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: your word is your promise
R and L stand for right and left, two sides

explanation.surface: A soldier's pledge to engage both flanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A warlord is a military commander, a fighting leader.

clue.text: Sadness revived after King deposed

indicators.note: a deposed monarch is removed from the throne, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: woke means came round, was revived
K is the abbreviation for King in chess

explanation.surface: Grief returns after a monarch is overthrown.
explanation.definitionFit: Woe is grief or misery, a synonym for sorrow.

clue.text: Useful resource? Preserves copy once it's blocked by old money

indicators.note: blocked by means stopped up by something inside it, so letters are inserted

parts.note: to bottle fruit is to preserve it
M is the abbreviation for money, as in M1 and M2
spit means an exact likeness, as in the spit of his father

explanation.surface: Jam-making copies an old recipe, a handy store when money is short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' only serves the surface. The question mark flags that something inexhaustible is useful only in a loose sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottomless pit is an endless supply, so the phrase suits a resource that never runs dry.
